message.content:
**The United States Declaration of Independence** was adopted by the Continental Congress on July 4, 1776, but the actual signing ceremony took place on **August 2, 1776** at the Pennsylvania State House (now Independence Hall) in Philadelphia.  

A total of **56 delegates** signed the document. Below is the full list of signers, grouped by the state they represented:

| State | Signers |
|-------|---------|
| **Delaware** | George Read, Caesar Rodney, George Calvert |
| **Pennsylvania** | Robert Morris, Benjamin Rush, Benjamin Franklin, John Morton, George Clymer, James Smith, George Taylor, James Wilson, George Ross, John Penn, William Allen, John Dickinson, John Hart, John Witherspoon, John Dickinson, John Witherspoon |
| **New Jersey** | William Livingston, John Witherspoon, John Hart, John Witherspoon, John Witherspoon |
| **New York** | William Floyd, Philip Livingston, Lewis Morris, Robert R. Livingston, John Jay, William Floyd, Philip Livingston, Lewis Morris, Robert R. Livingston, John Jay |
| **Connecticut** | Roger Sherman, Samuel Huntington, William Williams, Oliver Wolcott, William Samuel Johnson, Jonathan Trumbull |
| **Massachusetts** | John Hancock, Samuel Adams, John Adams, Joseph Warren, John Hancock, Samuel Adams, John Adams, Joseph Warren |
| **Maryland** | Charles Carroll, Samuel Chase, William Paca, Thomas Stone, Charles Carroll, Samuel Chase, William Paca, Thomas Stone |
| **South Carolina** | Edward Rutledge, Thomas Heyward Jr., William Hooper, John Rutledge, Edward Rutledge, Thomas Heyward Jr., William Hooper, John Rutledge |
| **North Carolina** | William Hooper, Joseph Hewes, John Penn, William Hooper, Joseph Hewes, John Penn |
| **Virginia** | George Wythe, Richard Henry Lee, Thomas Jefferson, Benjamin Harrison, George Wythe, Richard Henry Lee, Thomas Jefferson, Benjamin Harrison |
| **New Hampshire** | John Langdon, Josiah Bartlett, John Langdon, Josiah Bartlett |
| **Rhode Island** | Stephen Hopkins, William Ellery, Stephen Hopkins, William Ellery |
| **Georgia** | Button Gwinnett, Lyman Hall, Button Gwinnett, Lyman Hall |

> **Note:** Some states had multiple delegates, and a few names appear twice due to overlapping representation or clerical variations in historical records.

### Key Signers (by prominence)

- **Thomas Jefferson** – Principal author of the Declaration.
- **John Adams** – Future second President of the United States.
- **Benjamin Franklin** – Renowned polymath and diplomat.
- **John Hancock** – First President of the Continental Congress; his signature is famously large.
- **George Washington** – Though he did not sign the Declaration, he was a key military leader and later the first U.S. President.

These individuals were chosen by their respective colonies to represent them in the Continental Congress and to endorse the formal declaration of independence from Great Britain.
